AISettingHistoryResponse.description: Version history for one AI settings field, newest first.
AISettingHistoryResponse.title: AISettingHistoryResponse

AISettingRollback.description: Roll an AI settings field back to an existing history snapshot.
AISettingRollback.title: AISettingRollback

AISettingState.description: Currently active value of an AI settings field.
AISettingState.title: AISettingState

AISettingValueUpdate.description: Explicit save of an AI settings field — creates a new history snapshot.
AISettingValueUpdate.title: AISettingValueUpdate

BehaviorChoice.description: One answer a behavioral setting accepts.
BehaviorChoice.title: BehaviorChoice

BehaviorSettingCatalogEntry.description:
One setting, its choices, and what an unanswered device falls back to.

``default`` is always ``auto`` — Rally's own rule, the behavior that
predates this table — and it is carried so a client can mark a dropdown as
chosen or inherited without holding a second copy of the catalog.
BehaviorSettingCatalogEntry.title: BehaviorSettingCatalogEntry

DeviceAnnounce.description:
A device saying hello, and optionally naming itself.

The id is in the path rather than the body: the browser minted it and is
addressing its own record, which is a PUT to a known URL rather than a
create. Omitting ``label`` leaves a stored name alone, so a page that
merely says hello cannot overwrite one somebody typed.
DeviceAnnounce.title: DeviceAnnounce

DevicePreferencesResponse.description:
Every member's answers on one device, keyed by family member id.

Resolved, with the defaults filled in, for the same reason the notification
preferences are: a client that has to know the defaults to render a
dropdown is a second place for the defaults to live, and the two will
disagree. Keys are strings because JSON object keys always are.
DevicePreferencesResponse.title: DevicePreferencesResponse

EventNotifyResponse.description:
Per-recipient outcome.

"It worked" and "four phones buzzed" are different claims, and only this
shape can tell them apart — an attendee with no Pushover key is reported as
skipped rather than silently dropped, and one who turned event reminders
off is reported as muted. The manual notify button is filtered like every
other push, so it has to be able to say *"sent to Jon · Emma has event
reminders turned off"*.
EventNotifyResponse.title: EventNotifyResponse

EventResponse.description:
The stored series row, which is what the edit form reads.

Deliberately *not* the same shape as an occurrence: one is the rule, the
other is a dated instance of it, and collapsing them is how an edit ends up
applied to the wrong thing.
EventResponse.title: EventResponse

LLMConfigHistoryEntry.description:
One snapshot row from llm_settings_history, with the coupled value unpacked.

Snapshots saved before token limits were removed also carry ``max_tokens``
/ ``max_tokens_mode`` in their JSON; those keys are ignored.
LLMConfigHistoryEntry.title: LLMConfigHistoryEntry

LLMConfigHistoryResponse.description: Version history for the LLM configuration, newest first.
LLMConfigHistoryResponse.title: LLMConfigHistoryResponse

LLMConfigState.description: Currently active LLM provider + model configuration.
LLMConfigState.title: LLMConfigState

LLMConfigUpdate.description:
Explicit save of the LLM provider + model pair — creates a new history snapshot.

There is no output token budget to configure: Anthropic requests always use
the model's own maximum and local requests send no limit at all. Older
clients that still send ``max_tokens`` / ``max_tokens_mode`` are not
rejected — unknown fields are ignored (pydantic's default), so they're
simply dropped.
LLMConfigUpdate.title: LLMConfigUpdate

MealPlanReviewUpdate.description: Lightweight schema for submitting/editing a meal review.
MealPlanReviewUpdate.title: MealPlanReviewUpdate

MemberPreferencesResponse.description: One member's resolved answers on one device.
MemberPreferencesResponse.title: MemberPreferencesResponse

MemberPreferencesUpdate.description:
A partial set of answers for one member on one device.

Partial: a setting left out keeps its answer, so Settings saves one
dropdown without sending the others back. An unknown setting or value is a
422 rather than a stored preference nothing will ever read.
MemberPreferencesUpdate.title: MemberPreferencesUpdate

body_html.description:
The rendered note, built server-side so no page needs a renderer.

Both shapes travel together on purpose: the edit modal loads ``body``
into its textarea, and the page inserts ``body_html`` directly.
body_html.title: Body Html

NotificationKindOverview.description:
One row of the read-only *What Rally sends* list.

``audience`` is carried rather than derived client-side because it is the
answer to *"why didn't Jake get that?"*, and that answer belongs on the
same screen as the question. The three name lists are the state, split the
way a silent phone actually splits: hearing it, muted it, has no key.
NotificationKindOverview.title: NotificationKindOverview

NotificationOverviewResponse.description:
Every kind Rally sends, in catalog order.

``token_configured`` sits at the top because it is the first of the five
gates: with no application token nothing sends at all, and a list of
carefully configured recipients would otherwise read as working.
NotificationOverviewResponse.title: NotificationOverviewResponse

OccurrencePackingList.description: One packing list an occurrence brings, and the days it sits on.
OccurrencePackingList.title: OccurrencePackingList

OccurrencePage.description: Occurrences plus the sources that failed, so a view can say so.
OccurrencePage.title: OccurrencePage

OccurrenceResponse.description: One dated instance, which is what every view renders.

description_html.description:
The description as paragraphs, line breaks and links, built server-side.

Travels beside ``description`` rather than replacing it: the edit form
loads the raw text into its textarea, and the detail view inserts this
directly. Computed here, on the way out, so a description already sitting
in ``calendar_cache`` is formatted without a resync.
description_html.title: Description Html

reminder_display.description:
``1 hour before``; empty when the event has no reminder.

Empty only for ``None``: a reminder of ``0`` still fires, at the start,
and says so.
reminder_display.title: Reminder Display

start_date_display.description:
The first local date, ``Saturday, Oct 31, 2026``.

The day a one-time event's packing lists come off, as the ``Delete
event`` dialog names it.
start_date_display.title: Start Date Display

when_display.description:
The detail view's ``When`` row, without a zone.

``Friday, Oct 30, 2026 · 4:00 PM – 4:30 PM`` for a timed event within
one day; ``Friday, Oct 30 – Sunday, Nov 1, 2026 · All day`` for an
all-day one; and a date on each end for a timed one that crosses
midnight, ``Friday, Oct 30 10:30 PM – Saturday, Oct 31, 2026 6:15 AM``.
The notice's ``When:`` line (``notifications.when_label``) has the same
shapes and names its zone; this row never has.
when_display.title: When Display

OccurrenceResponse.title: OccurrenceResponse

PackingListBagOnListResponse.description:
A bag as one template or one day reads it, in reading order: outermost
first, then the bags inside each. ``parent_bag_id`` is always a bag on the
same list. ``changed`` says this list reads it differently from the level
above (``Reset`` shows). ``checked`` is grabbed, on a day.
PackingListBagOnListResponse.title: PackingListBagOnListResponse

PackingListBagReadingUpdate.description:
One list's reading of a bag: whose it is and what it goes in there.
Both fields, since a reading is whole; ``null`` is Everyone, and goes in
nothing.
PackingListBagReadingUpdate.title: PackingListBagReadingUpdate

PackingListBagUpdate.description:
A partial edit of a bag's household defaults. ``owner_id`` and
``parent_bag_id`` use ``UNSET``: left out, they stay; ``null`` clears
(Everyone, goes in nothing).
PackingListBagUpdate.title: PackingListBagUpdate

PackingListDayBagUpdate.description:
Grab a bag on one day, or read it differently there. Partial:
``owner_id`` and ``parent_bag_id`` use ``UNSET``, and setting either
writes the day's reading, copying the other from how the bag reads now.
PackingListDayBagUpdate.title: PackingListDayBagUpdate

PackingListDayCreate.description:
A packing list on a day, in one of three forms:

* ``packing_list_template_id``: the template itself on that day, kept in
  sync with it. ``pack_days_before`` is optional: left out (or ``None``)
  the day follows the template's, a number is the day's own.
* ``name``: a one-off, a templateless day with nothing on it yet.
* ``name`` and ``copy_from_template_id``: a one-off holding a copy of
  that template's items, with no link back.

A one-off has no template to follow, so it needs its own lead time. A
template id with a name or a copy, or none of the three, is a ``422`` —
the ``ShoppingItemCreate`` rule for ``store`` and ``store_id``.
PackingListDayCreate.title: PackingListDayCreate

PackingListDayEventLink.description: A calendar event a day belongs to: the occurrence's own title.
PackingListDayEventLink.title: PackingListDayEventLink

PackingListDayItemCreate.description: An item only one day has: a name, and optionally a note, owner and bag.
PackingListDayItemCreate.title: PackingListDayItemCreate

PackingListDayItemRef.description:
One item on a day: a template item (``template``) or one the day has
of its own (``day``). The two kinds come from different tables, so an id
alone does not say which.
PackingListDayItemRef.title: PackingListDayItemRef

PackingListDayItemResponse.description:
One item as it reads on one day, after the day's own changes.

``source`` says which endpoint edits it: ``template`` is a template item
(``/template-items/{id}``, ``id`` is the template item's), ``day`` is an
item only this day has (``/day-items/{id}``). ``changed`` marks a template
item this day has edited, which a later edit to the template no longer
reaches.
PackingListDayItemResponse.title: PackingListDayItemResponse

PackingListDayItemUpdate.description:
Check, edit, or both, for an item on one day — a template item or one
the day added. Partial, like an item update. An edit changes the item on
this day only; the template keeps its own.
PackingListDayItemUpdate.title: PackingListDayItemUpdate

PackingListDayReorder.description:
One group of a day's packing list, in one view, as it should now read.

``PackingListTemplateReorder`` for a day: every listed item takes the
group's owner or bag, on this day only, and the items are dealt back into
the places they held between them. Duplicates keep their first mention.
PackingListDayReorder.title: PackingListDayReorder

PackingListDayResponse.description:
The day's packing list itself: its items as this day has them, with
checks, and its bags with whether each was grabbed.
PackingListDayResponse.title: PackingListDayResponse

PackingListDayResync.description:
How much of a day to bring back in line with its template.

``items`` undoes the day's item edits, removals and additions (and puts a
bag back inside a bag the day took off, once that bag is back); ``all``
undoes every way the day differs: those, its order, its bag readings, its
checks, its label and its lead time.
PackingListDayResync.title: PackingListDayResync

PackingListItemCreate.description:
An item, on a template or on one day.

The bag comes as a name (``bag``), typed on the item: a name already in
the household's list, in any case, is that bag, and a new one joins the
list. ``bag_id`` names one that exists; sending both is a ``422``.
``owner_id`` is a family member; ``None`` is Everyone.
PackingListItemCreate.title: PackingListItemCreate

PackingListItemUpdate.description:
A partial edit. ``note``, ``owner_id``, ``bag`` and ``bag_id`` use
``UNSET``: left out, they stay; ``null`` clears (Everyone, No bag).
PackingListItemUpdate.title: PackingListItemUpdate

PackingListSuggestion.description:
An item name from history, with the owner and bag it last had.

``times_added`` is how many past days it was on a packing list.
PackingListSuggestion.title: PackingListSuggestion

PackingListTemplateCreate.description:
A new template. ``copy_from_template_id`` starts it with a copy of that
template's items (name, note, owner, bag, in order) and nothing else: the
name, description and lead time are this body's own. Copying happens only
here, at creation.
PackingListTemplateCreate.title: PackingListTemplateCreate

PackingListTemplateReorder.description:
One group of a template, in one view, as it should now read.

``view`` says what the groups are — owners or bags — and ``key`` which one
the items were dropped in (``None`` is Everyone, or No bag). Every listed
item takes that owner or bag, so dragging into another group is a reorder
whose payload names an item that used to live elsewhere: the
``ShoppingReorder`` contract, one level up.
PackingListTemplateReorder.title: PackingListTemplateReorder

PackingListTemplateResponse.description:
A template with its items, in order, and the schedule it repeats on
(``None`` when it does not).
PackingListTemplateResponse.title: PackingListTemplateResponse

PackingListTemplateScheduleUpdate.description: A partial edit. The rule is re-checked against the merged schedule.
PackingListTemplateScheduleUpdate.title: PackingListTemplateScheduleUpdate

PrepItemRefresh.description: Mark an item refreshed. Defaults to today in the family's timezone.
PrepItemRefresh.title: PrepItemRefresh

PrepItemUpdate.description:
Partial update. Nullable fields use the UNSET sentinel, so an explicit
``null`` clears the value while omission leaves it alone.
PrepItemUpdate.title: PrepItemUpdate

PurchasedPage.description:
One page of purchased items, plus the stores the Store chips offer.

``stores`` holds chip values — store ids as strings, and ``"anywhere"`` for
the catch-all — for every store with a purchase matching the current search,
*ignoring* the store filter. That is what the chips showed when they were
built from the whole archive in the browser, and answering it here keeps the
chips from depending on how many pages have been loaded.
PurchasedPage.title: PurchasedPage

RecurrenceDescribeRequest.description: An unsaved rule the form wants read back to it.
RecurrenceDescribeRequest.title: RecurrenceDescribeRequest

RecurrenceDescribeResponse.description: The rule in words. Empty when there is no rule to describe.
RecurrenceDescribeResponse.title: RecurrenceDescribeResponse

RecurrencePreviewRequest.description: An unsaved recurrence rule, asked what dates it would produce.
RecurrencePreviewRequest.title: RecurrencePreviewRequest

RecurrencePreviewResponse.description: The next few dates that rule lands on, earliest first.
RecurrencePreviewResponse.title: RecurrencePreviewResponse

SettingsResponse.description: All settings as a flat dict.
SettingsResponse.title: SettingsResponse

ShoppingReorder.description:
The new contents of one store group, in the order they should read.

A drag expresses both halves of a move at once — which store the item now
belongs to, and where it sits among that store's items — so one request
carries both rather than making the client issue a PUT and a reorder and
hope neither half fails on its own. ``store_id`` is the *destination*;
dragging across groups is just a reorder whose payload happens to include an
item that used to live somewhere else.
ShoppingReorder.title: ShoppingReorder

ShoppingSuggestion.description: One autocomplete match from the permanent item history.
ShoppingSuggestion.title: ShoppingSuggestion

get.description:
Dashboard: Regenerate Dashboard.

Trigger dashboard regeneration.

post.description:
Calendar: Describe Rule.

Read an **unsaved** rule back as the phrase the form would use.

The modal needs to describe a rule that does not exist server-side yet, and
the alternative is a second implementation of the vocabulary in JavaScript —
which is how the two drift. Same reasoning as
``POST /api/recurring-todos/preview``: one place knows what a rule means.

A malformed rule is *described* rather than rejected. The form asks this on
every keystroke, so a half-typed rule is the normal case, not an error; the
save path still validates through ``validate_rrule``.

Calendar: Calendar Sync Now.

Force a refresh of every external calendar.

The button behind this exists because the alternative to a cache is not
"always fresh" but "always slow": somebody who has just added an event
upstream needs a way to pull it in now without waiting out the interval.

get.description:
Calendar: Calendar Sync Status.

How fresh the cached calendars are, and which are failing.

delete.description:
Calendar: Delete Event.

Delete one occurrence, the tail of a series, or the whole event.

Each scope announces the deletion to the attendees. The notice is *planned*
before the delete and *sent* after it: a delete destroys the occurrence, the
attendee list and sometimes the event row, so there is nothing left to build
a message from afterwards — and announcing it beforehand would risk naming a
deletion that then failed.

A delete that would take a packing list off a day nobody else uses is a
``409`` with ``releases`` until ``release`` says whether the day stays
(#313); ``GET /delete-question`` asks the same without writing.

parameters.description: Whether a list this takes off a day stays there (keep) or goes (remove)
parameters.name: release

schema.description: Whether a list this takes off a day stays there (keep) or goes (remove)
schema.title: Release

get.description:
Calendar: Get Event.

The stored series row plus its overrides.

put.description:
Calendar: Update Event.

Edit an event at one of three scopes.

``all`` updates the series and **keeps existing overrides** — a soccer
practice the family already moved to Thursday must not snap back to Tuesday
because somebody corrected the title.

``following`` splits the series: the original is truncated with ``UNTIL``
and a new event carries the edited values forward, taking the overrides at
or after the split with it. Splitting on a *date* rather than an occurrence
index matters — an index shifts the moment an earlier occurrence is
cancelled.

Every scope announces itself to the attendees afterwards. Which occurrence
the notice names differs by scope, and that is the point: a change to one
Tuesday says that Tuesday, while a change to the series says the next one
people will actually turn up to.

Packing lists follow the same scopes (``packing_lists.set_series_lists`` /
``set_occurrence_lists``), and the event's packing list days are synced
before anything is committed. A move that would adopt a day already there
is a ``409`` unless ``adopt``; a move of an occurrence with packing lists
into the past is a ``422``. Taking a list off a day nobody else uses is a
``409`` with ``releases`` until ``release`` says whether the day stays.
Either way nothing is written.

parameters.description: Go ahead when a move adopts a packing list day
parameters.name: adopt

schema.description: Go ahead when a move adopts a packing list day
schema.title: Adopt

parameters.description: Whether a list this takes off a day stays there (keep) or goes (remove)
parameters.name: release

schema.description: Whether a list this takes off a day stays there (keep) or goes (remove)
schema.title: Release

get.description:
Calendar: Delete Question.

What deleting at this scope would ask: the packing lists it would take
off days nobody else uses, and the Keep or Remove question about them
(#313). ``releases`` is empty when it would ask nothing. Writes nothing:
the delete is tried and rolled back, so the answer is the delete's own.

post.description:
Calendar: Notify Event.

Push this event to its attendees now.

Defaults to the next upcoming occurrence, because "notify about the
dentist" almost always means the one that has not happened yet.

get.description:
Calendar: List Event Occurrences.

Occurrences of one series, so the UI can show what a change affects.

schema.title: Response List Event Occurrences Api Events  Event Id  Occurrences Get

get.description:
Family members: List Family Members.

List all family members.

schema.title: Response List Family Members Api Family Get

get.description:
Family members: Get Family Member.

Get a specific family member by ID.

Followed sports teams: List Followed Teams.

List every followed team and racing series, active or not.

schema.title: Response List Followed Teams Api Followed Teams Get

post.description:
Followed sports teams: Create Followed Team.

Follow a team or racing series.

delete.description:
Followed sports teams: Delete Followed Team.

Stop following a team. Announcement history is left alone.

put.description:
Followed sports teams: Update Followed Team.

Update a followed team. Omitted fields are left alone.

post.description:
Followed sports teams: Test Followed Team.

Fetch this team's next two weeks and report what came back.

The provider keys are undocumented and easy to get subtly wrong — a typo in
``team_key`` returns an empty schedule rather than an error, which would
otherwise present as "the sports section just never mentions the Stars".

get.description:
Meal planner: List Meal Plans.

List all meal plans ordered by date then meal type.

schema.title: Response List Meal Plans Api Meal Planner Get

post.description:
Meal planner: Create Meal Plan.

Create a new meal plan. Multiple plans per date are allowed.

get.description:
Meal planner: Get Meal Plans By Date.

Get all meal plans for a specific date (YYYY-MM-DD).

schema.title: Response Get Meal Plans By Date Api Meal Planner Date  Date  Get

get.description:
Meal planner: List Previous Meals.

List past meal plans (before today in the user's timezone).

Sort options:
- rating_desc: highest rated first, null ratings last
- date_desc: most recent first
- date_asc: oldest first

Every sort ends in ``id``: two dinners on one date, or two 5-star meals on
one date, otherwise tie, and offset paging over a tie can show a meal twice
or skip it.

``meal_type`` may be repeated to filter to any of the given types (e.g.
``?meal_type=Breakfast&meal_type=Lunch``); each value must be a known meal
type.

Searching and pagination are server-side because the client only ever holds
the pages it has loaded. ``total`` counts matches across every page.

parameters.description: Case-insensitive keyword matched against the meal, its notes, or its review.
parameters.name: search

schema.description: Case-insensitive keyword matched against the meal, its notes, or its review.
schema.title: Search

delete.description:
Meal planner: Delete Meal Plan.

Delete a meal plan.

get.description:
Meal planner: Get Meal Plan.

Get a specific meal plan by ID.

put.description:
Meal planner: Update Meal Plan.

Update a meal plan.

Meal planner: Review Meal.

Submit or update a meal review (rating and/or text).

get.description:
Daily notes: List Notes.

List notes from today onward, oldest first.

No upper bound: the planner runs to the end of the list, matching the Meal
Planner rather than capping at a week.

schema.title: Response List Notes Api Notes Get

post.description:
Daily notes: Create Note.

Create a note for a day that does not have one.

A date that already has a note is a `409` carrying that note's id, so the
modal can switch to editing it rather than refusing or overwriting. The
page checks its loaded list first; this is the guard for the case where two
people write the same day at once.

get.description:
Daily notes: List Previous Notes.

List notes for days before today, newest first.

The exact complement of the default listing: a note for today stays on the
Notes page and appears here only once the local date rolls over.

Searching and pagination are server-side because the client only ever holds
one page. ``total`` counts matches across every page, which is what the
results count reports — a per-page count would say "50 matching notes" no
matter how many there are.

parameters.description: Case-insensitive keyword matched against the note body.
parameters.name: search

schema.description: Case-insensitive keyword matched against the note body.
schema.title: Search

delete.description:
Daily notes: Delete Note.

Delete a note for today or a future day.

get.description:
Daily notes: Get Note.

Get one note.

put.description:
Daily notes: Update Note.

Update a note's text, its date, or both.

get.description:
Notifications: Notifications Overview.

Every kind Rally sends, its audience rule, and who currently gets it.

Read-only on purpose. The editor for a preference is the person's own
family member record — one editor for one piece of state — and this is the
screen that answers *"why didn't I get that?"* without making anybody open
four member modals to find out.

Packing lists: List Bags.

The household's bags, A to Z, each with its default owner and the bag it
goes in, and how many template items it holds.

schema.title: Response List Bags Api Packing List Bags Get

post.description:
Packing lists: Create Bag.

Add a bag, with no owner. ``409`` when an ownerless bag already has the
name, ignoring case.

delete.description:
Packing lists: Delete Bag.

Delete a bag. Whatever was in it goes to No bag rather than going with it,
and the bags that went in it go in nothing.

SQLite does not enforce the reference, so this is done by hand — items on
every template, every day's own items and readings, and history; the bags
inside it, by default and in every reading, and any day's record of a bag
taken out of it — the same reason deleting a
shopping store moves its items to Anywhere. Readings of the bag itself and
its grab checks go with it.

put.description:
Packing lists: Update Bag.

Partial: rename a bag everywhere it is used, or change the household's
default owner and the bag it goes in. A template or day that reads the bag
differently keeps its own reading.

``409`` when the name and owner it would end up with are another bag's;
an unknown owner or bag, or a bag put inside itself, is a ``422``.

get.description:
Packing lists: List Days.

Every day's packing list from today on, soonest first, with its items.

Puts every active schedule's template on its coming days first, the same
arrangement ``GET /api/todos`` has with recurring tasks: this is what the
Packing Lists page loads, so a schedule's days are there whenever anybody
looks. Counts the days that are over into item history too, for the same
reason (``logic.count_packed_days``).

schema.title: Response List Days Api Packing List Days Get

post.description:
Packing lists: Create Day.

Put a packing list on a day, starting with nothing checked.

Three forms (``PackingListDayCreate``): a template kept in sync, a blank
one-off, or a one-off holding a copy of a template's items. A day before
today is a ``422``: nobody packs for yesterday. A template already on that
day is a ``409`` carrying the existing day's id, so the page can open it
instead — the same shape Notes uses. A one-off never clashes: its name is
its own, and any number of them can share a date.

get.description:
Packing lists: List Previous Days.

Days before today, newest first: the archive.

The exact complement of the default listing, on the same
``today_local_str`` boundary. Searching and paging are server-side, and
``total`` counts every match, the same contract as previous notes. An
outer join, so a templateless day is in the archive too, found by its own
name.

parameters.description: Case-insensitive keyword matched against the packing list's name or label.
parameters.name: search

schema.description: Case-insensitive keyword matched against the packing list's name or label.
schema.title: Search

delete.description:
Packing lists: Delete Day.

Take a packing list off a day. Its template, if it has one, is untouched.

A day a schedule made stays off: the schedule never goes back over a date
it has already handled. Item history needs nothing undone, because a day
is only counted once its date is over, and a past day can't be deleted.

get.description:
Packing lists: Get Day.

A day's packing list: its items as this day has them, each with its check.

put.description:
Packing lists: Update Day.

Move a day's packing list to another date, relabel it, or give it its own
lead time (``pack_days_before``; ``null`` follows the template again, and
is a ``422`` on a templateless day, which has no template to follow).
Rename a templateless day (``name``; a ``422`` on a templated day).
Checks stay.

A label set here is the day's own from then on: a schedule's relabel
passes over it.

Packing lists: Update Day Bag.

Grab a bag on one day (``checked``), or read it differently on that day
only (``owner_id``, ``parent_bag_id``). Idempotent.

A reading is whole: setting one field copies the other from how the bag
reads on this day now. Returns the whole day. A bag not on the day is a
``404``; an unknown owner or bag, or a bag put inside itself, a ``422``;
an owner that would make it read as another bag's name and owner on this
day a ``409``; a past day a ``403``.

delete.description:
Packing lists: Reset Day Bag.

Reset: the bag reads as its template (or the household) has it again, on
this day. Idempotent; the bag's grab check stays.

post.description:
Packing lists: Remove Day Bag.

Take a bag off one day. Its items stay on the day, in No bag.

Each item in it moves to No bag on this day only: a template item through
the day's reading of it (so it reads ``(changed)``), one of the day's own
directly. The bags that went in it go in nothing on this day, each reading
recording the bag it came out of (``removed_from_bag_id``) so a resync can
put it back, and its grab check goes. The template, and every other day,
keep the bag. Item history is untouched: this is a move.

Packing lists: Check All.

Check everything on one day, its own items and its bags included.
Idempotent.

"Everything" is the day as it reads: an item it removed is not on it, so
nothing is checked for it, and a bag is grabbed only if it is on the day.

Packing lists: Create Own Item.

Add an item to this day only, after everything else on it.

Like an item added to a template, a new bag name joins the household's
bags and the item's name joins the autocomplete history.

delete.description:
Packing lists: Delete Own Item.

Delete an item only this day has.

put.description:
Packing lists: Update Own Item.

Edit or check an item only this day has.

post.description:
Packing lists: Reorder Day Items.

One group of a day's packing list, in one view, as it should now read.

The day's version of ``POST /api/packing-list-templates/{id}/items/reorder``:
the listed items are dealt back into the places they held between them,
so items in other groups keep theirs, and the day's whole order is stored
in ``item_order``. Template items and the day's own share that one order.

A drag within a group changes only the order, so nothing is marked
changed. A drag into another group gives the item that group's owner or
bag on this day only: a template item through the day's reading of it
(so it reads ``(changed)``), a day's own item directly. Duplicates keep
their first mention; an item not on the day is a ``404`` and nothing
changes; an unknown owner or bag is a ``422``; a past day is a ``403``.

Packing lists: Reset Day.

Uncheck everything on one day, its own items and its bags included.

Packing lists: Resync Day.

Bring one day back in line with its template (``logic.resync_day``):
``items`` undoes its item changes, ``all`` everything it does differently.

Idempotent. A past day is a ``403``; a templateless day, which has no
template to resync with, a ``422``.

delete.description:
Packing lists: Remove Day Template Item.

Take a template item off one day. The template, and every other day, keep it.

put.description:
Packing lists: Update Day Template Item.

Check, uncheck or edit a template item on one day. Idempotent.

An edit (``name``, ``note``, owner, bag) is this day's only: the template
keeps its own, and from then on a change to that item on the template no
longer reaches this day. Returns the whole day so the caller's progress
line comes from the server rather than from counting checkboxes.

Autocomplete from every item name somebody has typed, the shopping list's rules.

Substring, not prefix, so ``towel`` finds "Beach towel"; prefix matches
rank first, then by how many past days the name was packed on, then by
how recently it was typed. An empty ``q`` returns the most packed. Each
suggestion carries the owner and bag it last had, so the form can fill
them in when nobody has chosen yet.

Days it has already put on the calendar keep their dates either way: a
change to the rule only shapes days it has not reached yet. The label is
the exception — a schedule's label names its days, so a new one relabels
every day the schedule added from today on. Past days are the archive and
keep theirs. The rule is re-checked against the merged schedule, so a patch
that only changes the type still has to leave a schedule something can read.

post.description:
Packing lists: Create Template.

Create a template. ``409`` when the name is taken, ignoring case.

``copy_from_template_id`` starts it with a copy of that template's items,
each taken whole — name, note, owner and bag — in the source's order, and
its readings of bags (whose each is, what each goes in), so the copy's
bags read as the source's did. Only the items and those readings come
over: the name, description and lead time are the body's
own, and nothing links the copy back to its source, so a later edit or
deletion on either leaves the other alone. Copying is not typing, so item
history is untouched, as it is for a day's copy (``_create_one_off``). An
unknown source is a ``422``; the name check runs first, so neither failure
leaves anything behind.

delete.description:
Packing lists: Delete Template.

Delete a template, its items and its schedule.

Every day it is on is kept, made templateless first so it reads exactly as
it did (``logic.delete_template``): deleting a template never erases what
was packed or what is coming up.

Packing lists: Get Template.

put.description:
Packing lists: Update Template.

Packing lists: Update Template Bag.

Read a bag differently on this template: whose it is and what it goes in.

Every day the template is on reads it too, except a day with its own
reading of that bag. A bag not on the template is a ``404``; an unknown
owner or bag, or a bag put inside itself, is a ``422``; an owner that would
make it read as another bag's name and owner here is a ``409``.

delete.description:
Packing lists: Reset Template Bag.

Reset: the bag reads as the household has it again, on this template.
Idempotent.

post.description:
Packing lists: Remove Template Bag.

Take a bag off a template. Its items stay, in No bag.

The template's items in it go to No bag, which reaches every day it is on
except an item a day reads for itself. The bags that went in it go in
nothing on this template. Item history is untouched: this is a move.

Packing lists: Create Template Item.

Add an item to the bottom of the template. It is unchecked on every day.

A bag named for the first time joins the household's bags, and the name
joins the item history behind autocomplete.

Packing lists: Reorder Template Items.

One group, in one view, as it should now read — and who or what it is.

Every listed item takes the group's owner (``view: owner``) or bag
(``view: bag``), so a drag into another group is one request and cannot
half-apply. The template keeps one order: the listed items are dealt back
into the positions they held between them, in the new sequence, so items
in other groups keep their places. Duplicate ids keep their first mention;
an id not on this template is a ``404`` and nothing changes; an unknown
owner or bag is a ``422``.

The template's order wins: every day it is on from today on drops the
order it was arranged in by hand and reads in the new one.

post.description:
Shopping list: Create Item.

Add an item, deduplicating against the open list and recording history.

A store may be named instead of referenced by id, for scripted and voice
clients (Apple Shortcuts / Siri) that know names but not ids. An
*unrecognized* name is not an error — the item lands in the catch-all rather
than failing mid-dictation — and unknown names never auto-create a store.

Shopping list: Reorder Items.

Rewrite one store group's order, moving in any item that isn't there yet.

The client sends the destination group as it should now read, top to bottom,
and every listed item is assigned to ``store_id`` and numbered by its index.
That makes the endpoint idempotent and makes a cross-store drag the same
operation as a within-store one: the item simply appears in a payload for a
store it did not previously belong to.

The group the item *left* is deliberately not renumbered. Positions are only
ever compared, so the gap left behind changes nothing, and rewriting a second
group would double the rows this touches for no visible effect.

Only the items named in the payload are returned, in their new order — the
caller's own list is the thing it needs back. Completed items are usually
absent from it (they are not draggable and sort below the arranged ones
regardless), but naming one is allowed and moves it like any other row.
